solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Very little water among black stuff in Aussie swamp

indicators.note: something among other things sits in their midst, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: black stuff dug from a mine
a single letter, the abbreviation for water, is very little of it

explanation.surface: A trickle of water seeping through coal deposits in an Australian bog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very little' asks for the shortest form of water, its single-letter abbreviation. The word is Australian, so the clue flags it with 'Aussie'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowal is an Australian term, from an Aboriginal language, for a swampy depression or small lake.

clue.text: Dyspeptic

blocks.note: setter's reading: just the definition, since this is the word solvers write their own clues for

explanation.walkthrough: This was the Azed competition word: the puzzle gives only a definition, and entrants submit their own clues for it.
explanation.definitionFit: The rare adjective, from Greek roots for 'bad' and 'stomach', describes someone with a disordered digestion.

clue.text: Perfume dad got in on account of name, presented with a kiss

blocks.note: o' is a shortened form of on, as in 'o' nights'
an American informal word for father
a is short for account, as in a/c
a cross at the end of a letter stands for a kiss

explanation.surface: A father earns a perfume deal thanks to his name and seals it with a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dad got in on' puts dad straight after on; 'account of name' puts account after name.
explanation.definitionFit: Opopanax is a fragrant gum resin from a Mediterranean plant, long used as a scent in perfumery.

clue.text: Drunks like this will turn up after success at the races?

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the letters read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: a first-place finish for a bet on a horse

explanation.surface: Punters toasting a winner at the track end up the worse for drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Wino is slang for an alcoholic, especially a down-and-out drinker of cheap wine.

clue.text: Drunk let off – it's not much

indicators.note: food gone off is spoilt, so these letters lose their proper order

explanation.surface: A tipsy person is released, though it hardly matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let off' reads as being excused, but off signals a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a noun, a little is a small amount, which is what 'not much' describes.

clue.text: Guitar before start of liturgy, Dean's speciality?

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: slang for a guitar, especially an electric one

explanation.surface: A cathedral dean playing guitar before the service begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The dean is not a clergyman but Christopher Dean, the British ice dancer who won Olympic gold with Jayne Torvill.
explanation.definitionFit: An axel is a figure-skating jump, so it is fair to call it a skater's speciality, with the question mark owning the stretch.

clue.text: Transfer to adjust balance giving the old man energy

blocks.note: Latin, the old language, for man

explanation.surface: Moving money between accounts to keep things even gives Dad a boost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old man' looks like a father, but 'old' points to Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: To vire is to move funds from one budget heading to another, the verb behind virement in public accounting.

clue.text: A liberal philanthropist, however old

blocks.note: Bill Gates, who gives away a fortune through his foundation

explanation.surface: Describing a generous donor with progressive views, whatever his age.
explanation.definitionFit: Algates is an obsolete word meaning however or nevertheless, so 'old' marks it as archaic.

clue.text: East African, one resident in Siam oddly

indicators.note: a resident lives inside a place, so one piece is put within the other
done oddly means done strangely, so the letters come out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A Kenyan living in Thailand, a strange situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks like a call for odd letters, but here it shuffles the whole word with A inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Masai are a pastoral people of Kenya and Tanzania in East Africa.

clue.text: —— hobo's out of place in a bathroom – he met his end in one

definitions.text: he met his end in one

indicators.note: something out of a place has left it, so that letter goes
things out of place are disordered, so the remaining letters are shuffled too
in places one piece within the other

blocks.note: P is the map abbreviation for place
surface padding: sets the scene for the definition that follows

explanation.surface: A vagrant is wrongly lodged in a bathroom, where a famous man was killed.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash stands for the answer. 'Out of place' does double duty: P leaves the hobo, and what is left is jumbled with A set inside. Jean-Paul Marat was stabbed in his bath in 1793.
explanation.definitionFit: The French revolutionary was murdered by Charlotte Corday while bathing, so a bathroom is where he met his end.

clue.text: A blip? Thatcher might have had recourse to this abroad

definitions.text: Thatcher might have had recourse to this abroad

blocks.note: a blip is a light tap or knock

explanation.surface: A mere blip that Margaret Thatcher might have turned to on a foreign trip.
explanation.walkthrough: Thatcher is not the prime minister but anyone who thatches a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Atap is the Malay thatch made from palm leaves, so a roofer in South-East Asia would use it.

clue.text: Isis orants might have rattled these with endless noise

definitions.text: Isis orants might have rattled these with endless noise

indicators.note: rattled means shaken up, so these letters are jumbled
without an end means the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: the two words taken as written
the word without its final letter

explanation.surface: Worshippers of the Egyptian goddess shaking instruments and making a din.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus the shortened noise together rearrange to the two opening words. An orant is a figure at prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sistra, plural of sistrum, are metal rattles used in the worship of Isis in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: They'll save on heating bills – salon units I treated

indicators.note: something treated has been worked on and changed, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Fitting out salon premises with energy-saving measures.
explanation.definitionFit: Layers of lagging cut heat loss, so they reduce what you pay to warm a building.

clue.text: Oh-so-good football team, Roman, nets ball, being slightly crazy

indicators.note: to net something is to catch it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: pi is slang for pious, ostentatiously virtuous
a side of eleven, written in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A goody-goody Italian footballer scoring a goal and going a bit mad.
explanation.walkthrough: The ball goes inside the Roman, just before the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pixilation is the state of being pixilated, mildly unhinged or whimsical, as if led astray by pixies.

clue.text: Analyse in old Latin class extreme anxiety nation disposed of

indicators.note: something disposed of is got rid of, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: a state of alarm and dismay
taken as written, the part to be removed

explanation.surface: A schoolboy's panic in a Latin lesson, with a whole people swept away.
explanation.definitionFit: Conster is an old form of construe, the classroom task of parsing and translating a Latin sentence.

clue.text: Comprehends page penned by German writer

indicators.note: something penned is enclosed as in a pen, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: Günter Grass, author of The Tin Drum

explanation.surface: A reader takes in a page written by a German novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penned' looks like writing, matching the writer, but it means enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp an idea is to understand it fully, a common figurative synonym.

clue.text: Dry? Stick around for several pints, old style

indicators.note: one thing placed around another encloses it

explanation.surface: A teetotaller faced with an old measure of several pints.
explanation.walkthrough: Dry here means abstaining from alcohol, not lacking moisture.
explanation.definitionFit: A pottle was an old liquid measure of half a gallon, that is four pints.

clue.text: Crown circling prince I'll follow as hanger-on

indicators.note: to circle something is to go right round it, enclosing it

blocks.note: I, said to follow the prince, so it comes straight after him

explanation.surface: A courtier promises to trail behind a crowned prince, hanging around for favours.
explanation.walkthrough: RAS is the Ethiopian title (as in Ras Tafari); the head-crown wraps both the prince and the I that follows him.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasite in the social sense is someone who lives off others, a sponger or hanger-on.

clue.text: Have trouble breathing when doctor comes round

indicators.note: coming round something means encircling it

explanation.surface: A patient struggling for breath as the doctor visits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comes round' sounds like a house call or recovering consciousness, but it wraps the doctor around the link.
explanation.definitionFit: To gasp is to struggle for breath with short, convulsive intakes of air.

clue.text: Throaty sound from the belly, ultra distorted

indicators.note: a distorted thing is twisted out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A deep growl from the stomach, extremely warped.
explanation.definitionFit: A guttural is a consonant made in the throat, so the noun names a throaty speech sound.

clue.text: Name periodical brought up for 'sexually active'

indicators.note: in a down entry, brought up means read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: to name is to cite, as an example or a source

explanation.surface: Citing a journal that was raised as a source for a phrase about sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Gametic means relating to gametes, the sex cells, so it describes what is active in reproduction.

clue.text: Fine old blade, fad rarer arena's displayed with a flourish (13, two words)

indicators.note: a flourish is an extravagant wave, so the letters are flung into a new pattern

blocks.note: the words taken as written, apostrophe-s ignored

explanation.surface: A swordsman waves a fine antique sword around a rarely used arena.
explanation.definitionFit: An Andrea Ferrara is a high-quality broadsword, named after a famous sixteenth-century Italian swordsmith.

clue.text: Menial urged to work with day added on

indicators.note: put to work, the letters are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: A servant pressed to labour with an extra day on the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The day is added to the five letters before they are put to work, so it ends up in the middle of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A drudge is a person made to do dull, servile work, a lowly menial.

clue.text: What's displaying form of rut with age?

definitions.text: What's displaying form of rut with age?

indicators.note: a form of something is a version of it, so the letters take a new shape

explanation.surface: Asking what shows the furrows that come with getting older.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: ruts with age suggest wrinkles.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugate means wrinkled or ridged, and a skin creased by years shows exactly those furrows.

clue.text: Bow during mass unsteadily, revealing fleshy lumps

indicators.note: something done unsteadily wobbles out of its proper order
one thing during another sits within its span

blocks.note: musical direction to play with the bow

explanation.surface: Someone bowing shakily during a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is not a bend at the waist but the musical arco.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarcomas are malignant tumours of connective tissue, swellings in the flesh; the Greek root sarx means flesh.

clue.text: Bead fastener old James attached to one of netsuke's pair

blocks.note: the word contains two of this letter, so it is one of a pair

explanation.surface: An ornament of old James's linked to a Japanese carved toggle.
explanation.walkthrough: Netsuke are Japanese carved toggles, used in the same kit as the bead.
explanation.definitionFit: An ojime is a sliding bead on the cords of a Japanese inro, used to keep the case closed.

clue.text: Little bird: hard when it's caught by its predator?

indicators.note: something caught by another is held inside it

blocks.note: the natural enemy of small birds
standard abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A small bird in a tight spot once the cat has it.
explanation.definitionFit: Chats are small songbirds such as the stonechat and whinchat.

clue.text: What may be found in Rhone, flapping about

definitions.text: What may be found in Rhone, flapping about

indicators.note: flapping about means moving wildly, so the letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: the river's name taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird beating its wings in a French river.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the bird and also supplies the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Herons are wading birds that fish in rivers and flap slowly as they take off.

clue.text: Deserts, or nameless features thereof

indicators.note: nameless means without a name, so its abbreviation is taken out

blocks.note: first meaning: what one deserves, as in just deserts
sand hills found in a desert
standard abbreviation for name, the letter removed

explanation.surface: Arid wastes, or the unnamed landmarks found in them.
explanation.walkthrough: Deserts is pronounced like desserts here: rewards earned, not arid land.
explanation.definitionFit: One's dues are what one is owed or has earned, the same as one's just deserts.

clue.text: Loathe being taken in by backward personality? Acts as ringleader

indicators.note: something taken in is enclosed by what takes it
backward means read from right to left

blocks.note: Chambers gives ug as an old verb meaning to loathe

explanation.surface: A shy, self-effacing person is fooled and then leads the gang.
explanation.definitionFit: To fugle is to act as a fugleman, the soldier who stands in front as a model, so to lead others.

clue.text: Indian liquor, peaty by the sound of it

indicators.note: says the answer is heard rather than spelt like the word given

blocks.note: fenny means boggy, like peat land

explanation.surface: A drink from India with a smoky taste, like whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Feni is a spirit distilled in Goa from cashew fruit or coconut palm sap.

clue.text: Uxorious husbands abound there, principally, abroad!

definitions.text: Uxorious husbands abound there, principally, abroad!

indicators.note: principally means chiefly, so each word gives its chief, opening letter
abroad means scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order

blocks.note: the opening letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A wry remark that doting husbands are plentiful in a foreign place.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: the Mormon settlers of this US state were known for plural marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah was settled by Mormons who once practised polygamy, so husbands with many wives were common there.

clue.text: Garrison retreat: ruined number lost rebuilt with time

indicators.note: a thing lost is no longer there, so that letter goes
something rebuilt is put back together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A wrecked fort restored after losing its company, given time.
explanation.definitionFit: A reduit is an inner stronghold of a fortification into which a garrison can withdraw.

clue.text: E.g. raspberry feature some Manoir eaters knocked back

indicators.note: some means part of the words that follow, a run of their letters
knocked back means turned backwards, read right to left

blocks.note: the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: Diners at a country-house hotel downing a raspberry dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: Le Manoir aux Quat'Saisons is a famous restaurant near Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: An etaerio is an aggregate fruit made of many small drupelets, as a raspberry is.

clue.text: Formally repeat what's arranged in a meeting

indicators.note: arranged means set in order, so the letters are put into a new sequence

explanation.surface: Saying things twice for the record, as set out at a committee.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingeminate is a learned word for repeating or reiterating, from Latin geminare, to double.

clue.text: Dubious reading of Will's English in subject of inquiry

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

explanation.surface: A disputed line in a will becomes the focus of a legal investigation.
explanation.walkthrough: Will is not a legal document but William Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Caese appears in some editions of Shakespeare, a doubtful text that may be a misprint for cease or another word.

clue.text: Sea eagles sailors spotted in experience from stern

indicators.note: from the stern is from the back end, so the word reads backwards
something spotted in a place is seen inside it

blocks.note: to see is to undergo or experience

explanation.surface: Seamen catch sight of large birds astern, a familiar experience at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernes, or erns, are white-tailed eagles that hunt along coasts.
